newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-BEARDSLEY SYMBOLISES NEWCASTLE TITLE DRIVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SHOWCASE-BEARDSLEY SYMBOLISES NEWCASTLE TITLE DRIVE.

text.p: The confidence, exuberance and determination of Peter Beardsley's play in his 700th league and cup match symbolised everything about Newcastle United's challenge for the English title on Sunday.

Newcastle won a bruising, passionate Tyne-Tees derby against old rivals Middlesbrough 3-1 to regain their place at the top of the premier league, displacing Arsenal who held the position for two weeks.

Beardsley's performance personified all that Newcastle -- and for that matter their coach Kevin Keegan -- represents: hard work, flair, style and, clearly this season, some mental toughness and maturity.

Beardsley, the Newcastle skipper, hussled in midfield and worked tirelessly in front of goal. He had the confidence to take, and score from, a penalty kick after missing from the spot last week, and scored a goal of typically sweet invention, dancing through the defence, then placing a low shot wide of the keeper to virtually ensure Newcastle's win.
"After missing the penalty against Ferencvaros on Tuesday the gaffer never said a word about the penalty, not even `unlucky'. He never said anything, he just left it to me," said Beardsley.
"A lot of fans asked what would happen if we got another one, but I've always said I'll take it. I wasn't sure I would score, but luckily enough it went in."
Beardlsey hugged his six-year-old son Drew, one of the ball boys behind the goal, after he scored in what was a poignant moment in another magical personal day.

The 35-year-old former England forward may be in the autumn of his career but he is hoping to keep playing at the top level until he is 40. On Sunday's evidence, you would bet on him lasting till he was 50.

Keegan, whose side pulsates to the same kind of rhythm he himself displayed as a player, was full of praise for his skipper, and said he was surprised some Newcastle fans were beginning to question Beardsley's durability.
"I saw a letter in the local paper today saying he was finished. Well, I'd like about another five players who are finished if that's the case," he said.
"His enthusiasm has, and always will be, incredible, and always worth a place in your side.
"Great players like him write their own scripts. You felt he would get a hat-trick and he damn nearly did."

Beardlsey, who won two championship medals with Liverpool, opened the scoring with the 40th minute penalty and made it 2-0 after 69 minutes when he jinked through the Middlesbrough defence and scored from close range.
Robert Lee added Newcastle's third with his first goal for 18 matches, and Middlesbrough replied through Mikkel Beck in the 88th minute.
There were 11 different countries represented in the two teams assembled for around 65 million pounds sterling ($106.6 million) sterling, and the match was marked with little cameo conflicts.

Middlesbrough's Brazilian Emerson and Newcastle's Colombian Faustino Asprilla continually tangled, Newcastle's Belgian Phillipe Albert had a running fued with Middlesbrough's Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli.
But if Beardsley symbolised Newcastle's drive for a title they last won in 1927, Albert and Juninho, Middlesbrough's diminutive forward, symbolised the current standing between the two clubs.

They had an altercation in the second half with Albert towering almost 30 cms over the Brazilian. With Newvastle in first place and Middlesbrough in 15th after a poor recent run, that image left a lasting impression of Newcastle's superiority.
Keegan also played with three men at the back, as he did against Ferencvaros on Tuesday, with David Batty patrolling in front of them and winger Keith Gillespie dropping into right-back when needed.
"It's the first time I've played that but it won't be the last, though I don't know when you'll next see it," said Keegan.

No-one at St James' Park is getting carried away with Newcastle being top of the league -- they remember all too vividly what happened last season when they led the table for almost eight months, then finished second to Manchester United.
But Keegan was pleased afterwards. "We didn't touch the heights of Ferencvaros (4-0) or Manchester United (5-0), but this was a derby and called for other qualities and strengths.
